LESSON: SINGING GAMES- WESTERN STYLE

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two
Subject: CREATIVE ACTIVITIES FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENTS
Strand: Appreciation
Topic 3.1: Singing Games- Western Style
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 18

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Singing Games- Western Style, part of Appreciation in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two CREATIVE ACTIVITIES FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENTS.

Key inquiry question: How can you make a singing game interesting?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Singing Games- Western Style together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Digital literacy: The learner records the Western singing or sign singing game performances using digital devices and shares

with peers for feedback,

Values:
• Integrity: The learner observes language etiquette as they describe body movements in western style singing or sign singing

games.

• Unity: The learner works together with peers during group performances and rehearsals of Western singing or sign singing

games.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social Cohesion: The learner watches singing or sign singing games from different countries.

Link to other learning areas:

English, Kiswahili and Indigenous language Activities: The learners use the languages to describe colours of props and costumes

in Western singing or sign singing game performances.

Suggested learning resources.

Whistles, flags for signals, digital devices.
